identity.name: Submariner
identity.one_liner: The 2012-2020 no-date Submariner: ceramic bezel, maxi case, caliber 3130.

narrative.story: The 114060 brought the no-date Sub into the ceramic era two years after the Date version, pairing Cerachrom and the Super Case with the time-only 3130. narrative.collector_notes: Values sit below the 116610LN. There are no dial or bezel variants to chase within the reference, so condition drives the price.

identity.name: Cosmograph Daytona
identity.one_liner: The steel Daytona whose ceramic bezel and multi-year waitlists defined the 2016-2023 hype market.

narrative.story: Rolex put a black Cerachrom bezel on the steel Daytona in 2016, visually recalling the black-bezel 6241 of the 1960s and immediately dating the outgoing 116520. Demand outran supply for its entire seven-year run: authorized dealers kept multi-year lists and the watch traded at a large premium over retail throughout, peaking in early 2022. Discontinued in 2023 for the 126500LN, it remains the shorthand example of the retail-versus-grey-market gap.
narrative.collector_notes: White 'panda' dials carry a consistent premium over black. Check the bezel edge for chips and the warranty-card date; 2023-dated full sets mark the final production year.

identity.name: Cosmograph Daytona
identity.one_liner: The first Daytona with Rolex's own chronograph movement, produced 2000-2016.

narrative.story: The 116520 launched in 2000 with the new in-house caliber 4130, ending the Zenith era with a simpler architecture: fewer parts, a vertical clutch, and a 72-hour reserve. It spent sixteen years as the steel Daytona, spanning the model's shift from steady seller to allocation piece. Early examples with the 'APH' dial (a spacing error in COSMOGRAPH) and cream-aged subdials draw specific attention.
narrative.collector_notes: Early white dials age toward cream — original unrestored dials matter. With so many small revisions over sixteen years, serial-era consistency between watch, bezel, and papers is what separates good full sets.

identity.name: Submariner Date
identity.one_liner: The green-dial, green-bezel Submariner of 2010-2020 whose discontinuation pushed its market price far above the black model's.

narrative.story: Launched alongside the black 116610LN in 2010, the LV paired a green sunburst dial with a green Cerachrom bezel — the first all-green Submariner, following the green-bezel-only 'Kermit' 16610LV. Collectors named it the Hulk for the color and the heavy maxi case. When Rolex dropped it in 2020 without a direct all-green successor, secondary prices moved sharply upward and have stayed above the black model's since.
narrative.collector_notes: The dial shifts with light from deep green to near-black; photographs oversell the effect. Discontinuation made 2019-2020-carded full sets the sought-after configuration.

identity.name: GMT-Master II
identity.one_liner: The 2013-2019 blue-black GMT that proved a two-color ceramic bezel could be made in one piece.

narrative.story: The 116710BLNR carried the first two-color Cerachrom bezel — Rolex's answer to the assumption that a one-piece ceramic insert could not hold two colors. Blue-black was a new combination for the GMT line, and the watch pulled long waitlists on the Oyster bracelet with caliber 3186. Discontinued in 2019 for the Jubilee-equipped 126710BLNR, it keeps a following as the original Batman.
narrative.collector_notes: Sold only on the Oyster bracelet — a Jubilee example is a swap or the later reference. Bezel condition dictates price; the blue half of early inserts varies slightly in tone.

identity.one_liner: The 2023 update of the steel Daytona for the model's 60th year, with caliber 4131 and a metal-edged ceramic bezel.

narrative.story: Introduced at Watches and Wonders 2023 for the Daytona's 60th anniversary, the 126500LN reworked the case lines and framed the Cerachrom bezel with a thin polished-steel edge. Inside, the 4131 replaced the long-serving 4130, adding the Chronergy escapement and a redesigned rotor. The white dial kept its predecessor's market pattern: it is the harder allocation and the stronger trader of the two dials.
narrative.collector_notes: Differences from the 116500LN are subtle at a glance — the steel bezel lip, slimmer lugs, and reworked subdial rings. White dials command the premium; grey-market spreads narrowed from the 2022 peak but stay above retail.

identity.name: Cosmograph Daytona
identity.one_liner: The 1988-2000 automatic Daytona built on a reworked Zenith El Primero — the reference that started the Daytona waitlist.

narrative.story: Rolex's first self-winding Daytona used the Zenith El Primero as its base, slowed from 36,000 to 28,800 vph and reworked so heavily that roughly half the parts changed. The 40mm case, sapphire crystal, and glossy dials set the Daytona's modern shape, and demand outran supply almost immediately — the Daytona waitlist is a 16520-era invention. Collectors track it by dial marks, from early 'floating' Cosmograph text to inverted-6 subdials.
narrative.collector_notes: 'Patrizzi' dials — subdial rings oxidized to brown on circa 1994-95 examples — carry a premium, as do early floating-dial and four-line versions. Service dials and replacement hands are common; period-correct parts drive the price.

identity.name: GMT-Master
identity.one_liner: The GMT-Master produced 1959-1980, the longest-running GMT reference and the standard vintage Pepsi.

narrative.story: The 1675 carried the GMT-Master through two decades: early gilt chapter-ring dials with pointed crown guards, then matte dials, on calibers 1565 and later 1575. Its Pepsi bezel and long production made it the entry point of serious vintage Rolex collecting. Marlon Brando's bezel-less 1675, worn in Apocalypse Now, sold at Phillips New York in December 2019.
narrative.collector_notes: Dial and bezel-insert originality set the price; gilt and pointed-crown-guard early examples trade at multiples of 1970s matte watches. Check for correct-era hands and unpolished case lines.

identity.name: Submariner Date
identity.one_liner: The first Submariner with a date, wearing red 'Submariner' dial text for roughly its first six years of production.

narrative.story: The 1680 added a date and cyclops to the Submariner, and early production printed the model name in red — a detail dropped around 1975 when the text turned white. Collectors sort Red Subs into Mark I through Mark VI dials by font and depth-rating layout, with the early meters-first marks the most valued. The red dial era turned a production quirk into one of vintage Rolex's most recognized sub-categories.
narrative.collector_notes: Verify the dial mark against the serial range; redialed and service-dial examples are everywhere. Feet-first versus meters-first depth text and open versus closed 6s are the fast checks.

identity.name: Submariner
identity.one_liner: The no-date Submariner produced 1962-1989 — the longest-running Sub reference and the staple of vintage Rolex collecting.

narrative.story: The 5513 ran nearly three decades on calibers 1530 and 1520, spanning gilt gloss dials, matte dials with painted markers, and finally gloss dials with white-gold surrounds. That length of production created a catalog of collectible variants — 'Bart Simpson' coronets, meters-first depth text, serif dials — and a price ladder that runs from entry-vintage to six figures for early gilt examples. Roger Moore wore a modified 5513 in Live and Let Die.
narrative.collector_notes: Dial originality first: service dials with modern lume are common and cut value hard. Match the dial era to the serial, check bezel-insert correctness, and expect unpolished cases to command large premiums.

identity.name: Cosmograph Daytona
identity.one_liner: The exotic-dial 6239 that became the most famous chronograph in collecting after Newman's own example sold for $17.75 million.

narrative.story: The 6239 introduced the Daytona name in 1963 and moved the tachymeter from the dial to the bezel. A slow-selling 'exotic' dial option — Art Deco numerals, blocked subdials, a contrasting outer track — was later nicknamed for Paul Newman, who wore one given to him by Joanne Woodward. When Newman's actual watch sold at Phillips New York in October 2017, it set the record for any wristwatch at auction and repriced the entire exotic-dial market.
narrative.collector_notes: Dial authenticity is everything: exotic dials were made by Singer and have known fonts, step details, and subdial geometry. Most surviving 6239s wear standard dials — a genuine Paul Newman dial multiplies the value several times over.
